_about: Survey of the member teratology information services listed by ENTIS at https://www.entis-org.eu/centers, read 2026-10-03: whether each publishes a public page per medicine, and the sentence of its terms that governs reuse and linking. Sites that did not load are marked unclear, not no.

centres.name: Línea Salud Fetal
centres.institution: Centro Nacional de Genética Médica (CeNAGeM), ANLIS "Dr. Carlos G. Malbrán", Ministerio de Salud de la Nación
centres.website: www.anlis.gov.ar/inst/CeNaGeM/saludfetal/todo.htm (as listed by ENTIS; could not be opened, see notes)
centres.audience: public and healthcare professionals (per ENTIS centre page; not verified on a live site)
centres.notes: The centre has no separate ENTIS-listed website other than the ANLIS institutional domain. https://www.anlis.gov.ar/inst/CeNaGeM/saludfetal/todo.htm and the http version both failed to load (certificate error: 'unable to verify the first certificate'). The institutional page https://www.argentina.gob.ar/salud/anlis/cenagem (current ANLIS domain) was found via search but was not confirmed to contain the Línea Salud Fetal content or any per-medicine pages. Service appears to be phone/email only (0800 444 2111, saludfetal@renac.com per search). Cannot confirm publication of public medicine pages.

terms.quote: Tous les contenus presents sur le site sont couverts par le droit d'auteur.
terms.deep_links: Allowed, with a condition: "La creation des liens hypertextes pointant vers le contenu du site www.lecrat.fr est autorisee sous reserve d'etre accessible par l'ouverture d'une nouvelle fenetre" (link must open in a new window; embedding/framing the page inside another site is not allowed). Citation in scientific/medical communication is explicitly invited with a prescribed reference format ("CRAT. Centre de Reference sur les Agents Teratogenes. [Page name]. Available at: [URL]. (accessed [date])."); copying, downloading, scraping, or commercial reuse beyond citation requires written permission from the publication director or APHP legal affairs.

centres.notes: CRAT is the clearest case of a public per-substance register among the surveyed centres, with per-topic pages (pregnancy/breastfeeding/paternal) for most drugs, plus a curated teratogen risk list.

The service is described only on the ENTIS centre page and on ISCIII's institutional site (https://www.isciii.es/servicios/registros-enfermedades-raras); the specific sub-page https://www.isciii.es/QueHacemos/Servicios/RegistrosInformacionEnfermedadesRaras/Paginas/RiesgosEmbarazo.aspx returned only generic ISCIII site-wide navigation when fetched, not substance content.
other_material: https://revista.isciii.es/index.php/ecemc/en/article/download/728/790 (Boletín del ECEMC: annual SITTE/SITE activity report, PDF, includes statistics on teratogen consultations, not a per-substance public database)
https://www.isciii.es/servicios/unidad-tecnica-talidomida-inicio (ISCIII Thalidomide Technical Unit, related but distinct service)

terms.quote: queda prohibida su reproducción, distribución, comunicación pública y transformación, total o parcial, sin la autorización expresa del ISCIII
terms.deep_links: Not addressed specifically; general legal notice governs the whole isciii.es domain, no SITTE/SITE-specific terms found.

centres.notes: SITTE/SITE is a phone/email consultation service for professionals (SITTE) and pregnant women (SITE) run from within ISCIII; no evidence of any public, login-free page per medicine/substance was found despite searching ISCIII's site and Spanish search results. The 'legal notice' found is ISCIII's institution-wide notice, not specific to this service.

centres.name: Moeders van Morgen (TIS – Teratology Information Service), Lareb
centres.institution: Netherlands Pharmacovigilance Centre Lareb (Bijwerkingencentrum Lareb)
centres.url_pattern: Two patterns observed on lareb.nl: /tis-knowledge-screen?id=N (per-topic knowledge screen) and /mvm-kennis-pagina?naam=[Topic-Name]&type=TIS. The site appears to be a JavaScript-rendered app; WebFetch could only reliably retrieve a generic shell for these URLs, so pages were confirmed indirectly via indexed titles/snippets rather than full direct rendering.
centres.languages: Dutch (primary); some general background pages also in English (/en/)
centres.audience: public (patients / those planning pregnancy or breastfeeding), written to support patient-clinician discussion
centres.approx_substances: Unclear exact count; knowledge-screen ids run at least into the hundreds (e.g. id=455, id=229, id=168, id=56 all resolve to distinct topics), suggesting a large number of substance/topic pages, but no index listing a total was found.

sample_pages.isotretinoin: https://www.lareb.nl/tis-knowledge-screen?id=229 (indexed under isotretinoïne; page itself rendered as a generic shell under WebFetch and could not be independently confirmed beyond the search-engine snippet)
sample_pages.lithium: https://www.lareb.nl/tis-knowledge-screen?id=56 (indexed as 'Lithium tijdens de zwangerschap'; same rendering caveat as above)

other_material: https://www.lareb.nl/mvm-kennis (general background pages: medicine use with child wish/pregnancy, breastfeeding, male medicine use pre-conception, pregnancy dosing adjustments)
MediMama app (linked from mvm-kennis, not a web page)

terms.quote: None of the texts and reports shown on the site may be used, published, distributed and/or copied without written permission from Lareb.
terms.deep_links: Not specifically addressed; disclaimer permits personal use and citation with attribution but requires written permission for reproduction/redistribution.

centres.notes: A page specifically about valproate/valproic acid use by women in pregnancy was not confirmed; the only valproate-related Lareb page found via search was 'Valproinezuur gebruik door de man met kinderwens' (paternal pre-conception use), at https://www.lareb.nl/mvm-kennis-pagina?naam=Valproinezuur-gebruik-door-de-man-met-kinderwens&type=TIS&origString=... — this is about paternal exposure, not the general valproate-in-pregnancy page, so it is not given as the sample page. Because the site renders content client-side, automated fetches returned a generic page shell rather than the substance-specific text for the id-based URLs; confirmation here rests on search-engine-indexed titles, which is a weaker form of verification than directly reading the rendered page.

centres.name: RELIS (Regionale legemiddelinformasjonssentre) — Trygg Mammamedisin
centres.institution: Four regional centres: Haukeland universitetssjukehus (RELIS Vest), Oslo universitetssykehus HF Ullevål (RELIS Sør-Øst), St. Olavs hospital HF (RELIS Midt-Norge), Universitetssykehuset Nord-Norge HF (RELIS Nord-Norge)
centres.website: https://relis.no (professional-facing: Q&A/article database) and https://www.tryggmammamedisin.no (public-facing: pregnancy/breastfeeding medicine advice)
centres.url_pattern: tryggmammamedisin.no is organised by health condition, not by substance: /faq/gravid/[condition]/ (pregnancy) and /faq/ammer/[condition]/ (breastfeeding), e.g. /faq/gravid/svangerskapskvalme/, /faq/ammer/hostemedisiner-2/. No per-drug-name page pattern was found.
centres.audience: public (tryggmammamedisin.no: pregnant/breastfeeding women) and healthcare professionals (relis.no: Q&A submission and searchable answered-question/article archive)
centres.approx_substances: Not applicable — content is condition-based (about 10 common-ailment categories observed: cough, nausea, heartburn, constipation, allergy, fungal infection, pain relief, nasal congestion, cortisone creams, haemorrhoids), not a per-substance list.
other_material: https://relis.no/artikler/ (RELIS professional article/Q&A archive, searchable, useful to a pharmacist for specific drug-safety questions including in pregnancy, e.g. https://relis.no/artikler/27973/ and https://relis.no/artikler/47421)
https://www.tryggmammamedisin.no/hent-svar and /spor-oss (personalised Q&A intake, not published monographs)

terms.quote: Copyright © 2026 RELIS (generic footer notice only; no elaborated reuse/copyright clause was found on relis.no or tryggmammamedisin.no despite searching)
terms.deep_links: Not addressed; no dedicated terms-of-use, disclaimer, or legal-notice page could be located on either domain.

centres.notes: Despite targeted searches for valproate/isotretinoin/lithium pages on tryggmammamedisin.no, no dedicated per-substance pages were found; the service works by condition-based FAQ plus individualised question-and-answer requests, not published medicine monographs. RELIS's professional side (relis.no) does publish a large searchable archive of previously answered drug-safety questions (useful to a pharmacist) but this is a Q&A archive, not one page per medicine.

centres.name: Terafar – İzmir Katip Çelebi University Teratology Information, Training and Research Center
centres.institution: İzmir Katip Çelebi University, Atatürk Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi (Clinical Pharmacology and Toxicology Unit)
centres.languages: Turkish (site title and pages seen are in Turkish)
other_material: https://terafar.ikcu.edu.tr/Duyuru/37790/teratojenite-danismanligi-calistayi (announcement about a teratogenicity counselling workshop, not a medicine-information page)
https://terafar.ikcu.edu.tr/Iletisim/1167 (contact page)
centres.notes: Could not load the live site directly: every WebFetch attempt (https and http) failed with a TLS certificate error ('unable to verify the first certificate'), so the site's structure could not be verified first-hand. Google-indexed pages for this domain found only an announcements page and a contact page; targeted searches for valproate/isotretinoin/lithium content on this domain returned no results. Based on available evidence this looks like a university consultation unit rather than a public medicine-information database, but this is marked 'unclear' rather than 'no' because the site itself could not be opened to check.

centres.name: Trabzon-TIS (Karadeniz Technical University Teratology Information Service)
centres.institution: Karadeniz Technical University Faculty of Medicine
centres.notes: The domain www.ktupharmacology.com did not resolve on repeated attempts (DNS failure: 'getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND www.ktupharmacology.com') tried over both http and https on 2026-10-03. Web search for the domain's content returned no cached pages beyond academic references describing the service in general terms. The site appears to be currently offline or the domain has lapsed; cannot determine whether it ever published per-medicine pages.

centres.name: UK Teratology Information Service (UKTIS); public-facing arm: bumps (Best Use of Medicines in Pregnancy)
centres.institution: Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
centres.url_pattern: Public (bumps): medicinesinpregnancy.org/leaflets-a-z/[substance-slug]/. Professional (UKTIS): uktis.org/monographs/use-of-[substance]-in-pregnancy/ — summary visible to all, full monograph text behind NHS healthcare-professional login ('You need to be logged in to see the full monograph').
centres.languages: English for leaflets and monographs; a small set of patient-education animations also offered in Arabic, Urdu, Polish, Slovak and Spanish
centres.audience: public / patients (bumps leaflets, full text, no login) and healthcare professionals (UKTIS monographs, summary public, full text login-only)
centres.approx_substances: Not precisely counted; the bumps Leaflets A-Z index lists dozens of named substances/forms (confirmed entries include three separate valproate-form leaflets, two retinoid/isotretinoin leaflets, and lithium), but no total count was stated on the pages read.

sample_pages.valproate: https://www.medicinesinpregnancy.org/leaflets-a-z/sodium-valproate/ (confirmed: public, no login, about sodium valproate in pregnancy)
sample_pages.isotretinoin: https://www.medicinesinpregnancy.org/leaflets-a-z/isotretinoin-tablets/ (confirmed: public, no login, about isotretinoin capsules in pregnancy)
sample_pages.lithium: https://www.medicinesinpregnancy.org/leaflets-a-z/lithium/ (confirmed: public, no login, about lithium in pregnancy)

other_material: https://uktis.org/monographs/use-of-sodium-valproate-in-pregnancy/, https://uktis.org/monographs/use-of-isotretinoin-in-pregnancy/, https://uktis.org/monographs/use-of-lithium-in-pregnancy/ (professional monograph summaries, public; full text login-only for NHS healthcare professionals)
www.toxbase.org (referenced as the full literature-review resource, registration required; not independently verified in this survey)

terms.quote: This material may be freely reproduced for education and not for profit purposes within the UK National Health Service as long as the service is acknowledged in any work produced.
terms.class: citation allowed (NHS non-profit education only; commercial reproduction forbidden without written permission)
terms.deep_links: Not specifically addressed; the notice governs reproduction of 'the website' and 'material' generally, with no separate statement about linking to individual leaflet/monograph pages.

centres.notes: UKTIS and bumps are two sides of the same service (same NHS Trust): bumps leaflets are plain-language and fully public; UKTIS monographs are the underlying professional evidence reviews, publicly summarised but gated behind an NHS professional login for full text, as the task anticipated.
